metadata.title: KSW: Khmer Stop Word based Dictionary for Keyword Extraction
metadata.description: This paper introduces KSW, a Khmer-specific approach to keyword extraction that leverages a specialized stop word dictionary. Due to the limited availability of natural language processing resources for the Khmer language, effective keyword extraction has been a significant challenge. KSW addresses this by developing a tailored stop word dictionary and implementing a preprocessing methodology to remove stop words, thereby enhancing the extraction of meaningful keywords. Our experiments demonstrate that KSW achieves substantial improvements in accuracy and relevance compared to previous methods, highlighting its potential to advance Khmer text processing and information retrieval. The KSW resources, including the stop word dictionary, are available at the following GitHub repository: (https://github.com/back-kh/KSWv2-Khmer-Stop-Word-based-Dictionary-for-Keyword-Extraction.git).

metadata.title: The Transmission and Interpretation of Performing Arts Traditions in Tamil Palm Leaf Manuscripts
metadata.description: Tamil palm leaf manuscripts stand as enduring monuments to a rich and continuous intellectual tradition, serving not merely as historical documents but as living archives of Tamil civilization’s multifaceted understanding of humanity. This paper undertakes a humanities-focused case study to explore the profound cultural, philosophical, and societal significance embedded within these fragile artifacts. Moving beyond their material form, we examine how these manuscripts encapsulate and transmit knowledge across diverse domains, including literature, medicine, philosophy (such as Saiva Siddhanta and Siddha thought), astronomy, and social practices. Through a comparative analysis with other historical records and a detailed examination of their content, this paper highlights their unparalleled role in shaping Tamil identity, preserving indigenous knowledge systems, and reflecting unique worldviews. The ”results” of this study manifest as deeper insights into historical modes of thought, ethical frameworks, and the human quest for meaning within a specific cultural context, making their preservation and scholarly engagement a critical endeavor for understanding the broader human narrative.

metadata.title: Palm Leaf Manuscript of Tirukkural (Adhikaram 4: Verses 31–40)
metadata.description:
This item is a high-resolution digitized image of a traditional Tamil palm-leaf manuscript containing verses 31–40 from Adhikaram 4 (Aṟaṉ Valiyuruttal – The Assertion of Virtue) of the Tirukkural, authored by Thiruvalluvar.

The manuscript is engraved on processed palm leaves using a stylus, a characteristic feature of South Indian manuscript traditions. The folio displays two binding holes used for stringing the leaves together, along with neatly inscribed Tamil script arranged in linear format. Minor surface wear, ink darkening, and marginal scribal notations are visible, indicating its age and usage.

This manuscript represents the long-standing transmission of Tamil ethical literature through palm-leaf tradition prior to the advent of print culture. It is a valuable resource for the study of textual transmission, paleography, and classical Tamil philosophy.

metadata.title: Palm Leaf Manuscript of Tirukkural (Adhikaram 46: Verses 451–460)
metadata.description:
This item is a digitized image of a traditional Tamil palm-leaf manuscript containing verses 451–460 from Adhikaram 46 (Siṟṟiṉam Cērāmai – Avoiding Mean Company) of the Tirukkural, composed by Thiruvalluvar. This chapter belongs to the Poruṭpāl (Book of Wealth) section and emphasizes the importance of avoiding association with individuals of low character, unethical conduct, or harmful influence. The verses teach that a person's reputation, wisdom, and success are greatly affected by the company they keep.

The manuscript is inscribed on processed palm leaf using a stylus, characteristic of the classical South Indian manuscript tradition. The folio generally displays central binding holes for stringing, finely incised Tamil script arranged in linear form, and visible signs of aging such as surface wear, minor fissures, and darkened lettering. Marginal markings and slight irregularities indicate manual scribal transmission and continued historical handling.

This manuscript represents the enduring preservation and transmission of Tamil ethical, social, and political thought through palm-leaf tradition prior to print culture. It serves as a valuable resource for research in classical Tamil literature, manuscriptology, paleography, ethics, and cultural heritage studies.
